draft.title: The Fair Work Act 2009
card: The Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) is the main law for workplaces in Australia. It covers most private sector employees and employers across the country.
It sets the National Employment Standards (NES). These are 11 minimum entitlements that apply to every employee it covers.
The NES include annual leave, personal/carer's leave, parental leave and a maximum of 38 ordinary weekly hours for a full-time employee. Extra hours must be reasonable.
An employment contract, award or agreement cannot give an employee less than the NES. It can give more.
draft.remember: The Fair Work Act sets the minimum entitlements that every covered employee must get, and a contract can only add to them.

a.q: Zane starts a full-time job. His contract says he gets no annual leave. What is the legal effect of this term?
opts: It cannot override his NES leave entitlement
It is valid because Zane signed the contract
It is valid if his employer pays a higher wage
It applies only until his probation period ends
a.why: The NES are minimum entitlements that a contract cannot take away. Signing the contract does not remove them, so the term has no effect on Zane's right to annual leave.
a.clue: Can a contract give less than the NES?

b.q: Priya's employer in Newcastle offers her a contract with more annual leave than the NES requires. Which statement about this is correct?
opts: It is lawful, because the NES set only a minimum
It is unlawful, because the NES set a fixed amount
It is lawful only if the Fair Work Commission approves
It is unlawful, because it treats other staff unequally
b.why: The NES are a floor, not a ceiling, so an employer can give more than they require. The tempting idea that the NES fix the amount is wrong, because the Act only stops terms that give less.
b.clue: Think about whether the NES are a minimum or a fixed amount.

a.best: It cannot override his NES leave entitlement

b.best: It is lawful, because the NES set only a minimum

problems.detail: The card says the NES are 11 minimum entitlements. Since amendments in December 2023 added limits on fixed-term contracts, the Fair Work Ombudsman describes 12 NES. The number is likely out of date. It is safer to drop the number or update it.
'11 minimum entitlements that apply to every employee it covers' is misleading. Some NES entitlements, such as annual leave and paid personal/carer's leave, do not apply to casual employees.
'Minimum entitlements that every covered employee must get' repeats the overstatement. Casual employees covered by the Act do not get every NES entitlement, such as annual leave.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer. The card's count of '11' NES is likely out of date (now 12), and the card and remember line wrongly suggest every NES entitlement applies to every covered employee, including casuals.
